note: Mastering English Library dictionary. Definitions, examples and Arabic by Mastering English Library. Levels: CEFR-J Wordlist (Tono Lab, TUFS) and Octanove Vocabulary Profile (CC BY-SA 4.0). IPA: ipa-dict (MIT).

senses.def: used by a speaker or writer to talk about themselves
ex: I am a student.
I like pizza.

mistake.wrong: me and my friend went home.
mistake.right: My friend and I went home.
mistake.note: Use 'I' (not 'me') as the subject, and write it with a capital letter.

senses.def: a small picture on a screen that you click to open a program
ex: Click the icon to open the file.
The app icon is in the corner.

senses.def: a famous person or thing that is a symbol of something
ex: She is a fashion icon.

senses.def: extremely cold
ex: An icy wind blew across the field.
The water was icy.

senses.def: covered with ice
ex: The roads are icy this morning.

senses.def: an official card or document that shows who you are
ex: Please show your ID at the door.
You need photo ID to open an account.

senses.def: a plan or thought that comes into your mind
ex: That's a good idea.
I have an idea for dinner.

senses.def: an opinion or belief about something
ex: I have no idea what he means.

senses.def: exactly the same
ex: The twins wear identical clothes.
The two pictures are identical.

mistake.wrong: This bag is identical as mine.
mistake.right: This bag is identical to mine.

senses.def: an official document that shows who you are
ex: Please bring some form of identification.
He showed his identification to the guard.

senses.def: the act of recognising or naming someone or something
ex: The identification of the problem was quick.

senses.def: to recognise someone or something and say who or what they are
ex: Can you identify the man in the photo?
Doctors identified the cause of the illness.

senses.def: who a person is, or the qualities that make them different from others
ex: The police kept his identity secret.
Language is part of our cultural identity.

senses.def: a set of beliefs and ideas, especially political ones, that a group follows
ex: The party follows a strict ideology.
They disagree with his political ideology.

senses.def: a person who does something very stupid (an insulting word)
ex: I felt like an idiot when I forgot her name.
Don't be an idiot!

senses.def: not being used or not doing any work
ex: The factory stood idle for months.
He sat idle all afternoon.

senses.def: not willing to work
ex: He's an idle boy who never studies.

senses.def: if an engine idles, it runs slowly without moving the vehicle
ex: The engine idled outside the shop.

senses.def: a famous person who is greatly admired
ex: The singer is a teen idol.
He was my boyhood idol.

senses.def: used to say that one thing depends on another
ex: If it rains, we will stay at home.
I'll help if you want.

senses.def: used to talk about two possibilities, like 'whether'
ex: I don't know if she is at home.

mistake.wrong: If it will rain tomorrow, we stay home.
mistake.right: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
mistake.note: After 'if', use the present simple for the future, not 'will'.

senses.def: a lack of knowledge or information about something
ex: His ignorance of the law caused problems.
She admitted her ignorance.

senses.def: not knowing facts or information that you should know
ex: He is ignorant of the rules.
Don't be so ignorant.

senses.def: to pay no attention to someone or something
ex: She ignored his message.
Don't ignore the warning signs.

senses.def: not well; having a disease or health problem
ex: She is ill and cannot come to work.
He felt ill after lunch.

senses.def: not allowed by the law
ex: It is illegal to drive without a licence.
Selling these drugs is illegal.

senses.def: in a way that is against the law
ex: The car was illegally parked.
They entered the country illegally.

senses.def: a disease, or the state of being ill
ex: She missed school because of illness.
He died after a long illness.

senses.def: a picture, especially one on a screen
ex: The image on the screen was very clear.
She saved the image to her phone.

senses.def: the general opinion people have about a person or company
ex: The company wants to improve its image.

senses.def: existing only in your mind, not real
ex: The child has an imaginary friend.
The story is set in an imaginary world.

senses.def: the ability to form ideas and pictures in your mind
ex: Children have a wild imagination.
Use your imagination to write a story.

senses.def: a copy of something, or the act of copying
ex: The bag is a cheap imitation.
Children learn through imitation.

senses.def: happening or done at once, without delay
ex: The new rules take immediate effect.
I need an immediate answer.

senses.def: nearest in time, space or relationship
ex: Only my immediate family came.

senses.def: at once, without waiting
ex: Call me immediately.
She answered immediately.

senses.def: extremely large or great
ex: The new bridge is of immense size.
She felt immense pride.

senses.def: to a very great degree
ex: I enjoyed the concert immensely.
He is immensely popular.

senses.def: a person who comes to live in a different country
ex: Her parents were immigrants from Egypt.
The city has many immigrants.

senses.def: the act of coming to live in a different country
ex: The government wants to control immigration.
Show your passport at immigration.

senses.def: not following accepted ideas about what is right and good
ex: Many people think lying is immoral.
It's immoral to cheat.

senses.def: living or lasting forever
ex: In the story, the gods are immortal.
His music made him immortal.

senses.def: the ability to live forever
ex: Some people dream of immortality.
The poet won immortality through his work.

senses.def: without any fault or mistake
ex: She has impeccable manners.
His English is impeccable.

senses.def: in a perfect way, without any mistakes
ex: The waiters were impeccably dressed.
She behaved impeccably.

senses.def: something that makes it difficult to do or achieve something
ex: Lack of money is an impediment to progress.

senses.def: a physical problem that makes speaking difficult
ex: He has a speech impediment.

senses.def: the form of a verb used to give an order
ex: 'Sit down' is an imperative.

senses.def: extremely important and urgent
ex: It is imperative that you arrive on time.
Quick action is imperative.

senses.def: to pretend to be someone else, to trick people or to be funny
ex: He was arrested for impersonating a police officer.
She can impersonate famous singers.

senses.def: a tool or piece of equipment, especially for farming or gardening
ex: Farmers used simple wooden implements.

senses.def: to start using a plan, idea or system
ex: The school will implement the new rules in September.
They failed to implement the plan.

senses.def: to show that someone is involved in something bad, especially a crime
ex: The evidence implicated two officials.
He was implicated in the fraud.

senses.def: to suggest something without saying it directly
ex: Are you implying that I am lying?
His silence implied agreement.

senses.def: to bring goods into a country to sell them
ex: The country imports most of its oil.
They import cars from Japan.

senses.def: to copy data into a computer program from another source
ex: You can import photos from your phone.

senses.def: having great value or effect; needing attention
ex: Education is very important.
It's important to drink water.

senses.def: having a lot of power or influence
ex: She is an important person in the company.

mistake.wrong: It is important that to sleep well.
mistake.right: It is important to sleep well.
mistake.note: Use 'it is important to + verb', or 'it is important that + clause', not both.

senses.def: to make people accept a rule, tax or opinion
ex: The government imposed a new tax.
Parents shouldn't impose their opinions on children.

senses.def: something unfair or too much that you ask someone to accept or do
ex: I hope it's not too much of an imposition.
The imposition of new taxes upset many people.

senses.def: not able to happen or be done
ex: It's impossible to finish by noon.
That seems impossible.

senses.def: a person who organises concerts, plays or other entertainment
ex: The impresario arranged a tour for the orchestra.

senses.def: feeling admiration or respect for someone or something
ex: I was impressed by her speech.
The teacher was impressed with my work.

mistake.wrong: I was impressed from his speech.
mistake.right: I was impressed by his speech.

senses.def: the opinion or feeling you have about someone or something
ex: He made a good impression on the manager.
My first impression was that she was shy.

senses.def: an act of copying a person's voice or way of behaving
ex: He does a funny impression of the teacher.

senses.def: causing admiration because of being very good, large or skilled
ex: Her exam results were impressive.
It's an impressive building.

senses.def: the state of being in prison, or the act of putting someone there
ex: He was sentenced to five years' imprisonment.
The crime carries life imprisonment.

senses.def: better than before
ex: The phone has an improved camera.
We have an improved version of the app.

senses.def: a change that makes something better, or the act of getting better
ex: There has been a big improvement in his English.
The house needs some improvements.

senses.def: a sudden strong wish to do something without thinking
ex: I bought it on impulse.
She felt an impulse to laugh.

senses.def: doing things suddenly without thinking about the results
ex: He is an impulsive buyer.
It was an impulsive decision.

senses.def: inside a place, container or area
ex: The keys are in my bag.
She lives in London.

senses.def: used with months, years, seasons and parts of the day
ex: My birthday is in May.
We eat dinner in the evening.

senses.def: into a room, building or place
ex: Come in and sit down.
Is the manager in today?

mistake.wrong: I will see you in Monday.
mistake.right: I will see you on Monday.
mistake.note: Use 'on' with days of the week, and 'in' with months, years and seasons.

senses.def: not good enough or not enough for a purpose
ex: The school has inadequate equipment.
Her salary is inadequate for a family.

senses.def: a substance that gives a sweet smell when burnt
ex: The room smelled of incense.

senses.def: something that encourages you to do something
ex: Prizes are an incentive to work harder.
There is no incentive to save money.

senses.def: something that happens, especially something unpleasant
ex: Police are investigating the incident.
There was a strange incident at school.

senses.def: a cut made in something, especially in the body during an operation
ex: The surgeon made a small incision in his chest.

senses.def: used to show that someone or something is part of a group
ex: Everyone came, including my uncle.
The price is £50, including tax.

senses.def: the money that a person or business earns
ex: She has a high income.
Many families have a low income.

senses.def: more and more as time passes
ex: It is increasingly difficult to find a flat.
Increasingly, people are shopping online.

senses.def: so strange that it is difficult to believe
ex: It's incredible that he survived.
He told an incredible story.

senses.def: extremely good or large
ex: The view was incredible.

senses.def: extremely
ex: The test was incredibly difficult.
She is incredibly kind.

senses.def: a person who currently has an official position
ex: The incumbent won the election again.

senses.def: holding an official position at the present time
ex: The incumbent president will speak tonight.

senses.def: feeling grateful to someone for their help
ex: I am deeply indebted to my teacher.

senses.def: owing money to someone
ex: The firm is heavily indebted to the bank.

senses.def: used to stress that something is true, or to give extra emphasis after 'very'
ex: Thank you very much indeed.
It was indeed a great party.

senses.def: for a time with no fixed end
ex: The match was postponed indefinitely.
You cannot stay here indefinitely.

senses.def: not needing help or control from others
ex: She is very independent.
Teenagers want to be independent.

senses.def: ruling itself, not controlled by another country
ex: The country became independent in 1962.

senses.def: an alphabetical list at the back of a book showing where things are found
ex: Look up the word in the index.
The book has a long index.

senses.def: a number that shows the level or rate of something
ex: The price index rose last month.

senses.def: not interested in or caring about something
ex: He seemed indifferent to our problems.
She gave an indifferent shrug.

senses.def: angry because something seems unfair or insulting
ex: She was indignant at the accusation.
He gave an indignant reply.

senses.def: a careless act or remark that shows poor judgment
ex: A youthful indiscretion cost him his job.

senses.def: relating to one person or thing, not to a group
ex: Each student gets individual attention.
We sell individual portions.

senses.def: different from others in an interesting way
ex: She has an individual style.

senses.def: one person, considered separately from a group
ex: Every individual has rights.

senses.def: the belief that each person's freedom and choices matter more than those of a group
ex: Western culture often values individualism.

senses.def: the qualities that make a person different from others
ex: Teenagers often show their individuality through clothes.
She wants to express her individuality.

senses.def: to cause something to happen
ex: The drug induces sleep.
Doctors induced labour.

senses.def: to persuade someone to do something
ex: Nothing could induce her to leave.

senses.def: an introduction to a new job or organisation
ex: New staff attend an induction on their first day.

senses.def: the act of causing something to happen
ex: The induction of labour is sometimes needed.

senses.def: to allow yourself to have something enjoyable that may not be good for you
ex: I indulged in a large piece of cake.
She likes to indulge herself on holiday.

senses.def: to give someone everything they want
ex: Grandparents often indulge their grandchildren.

senses.def: the act of allowing yourself or others to enjoy something, often too much
ex: Chocolate is my one indulgence.
His indulgence spoilt the children.

senses.def: connected with industry or factories
ex: The city has a large industrial area.
Industrial waste pollutes the river.

senses.def: the production of goods in factories, or a group of businesses of one kind
ex: The car industry employs many people.
She works in the music industry.

mistake.wrong: My father works in an industry of cars.
mistake.right: My father works in the car industry.
mistake.note: Use a noun before 'industry' (the car industry) instead of 'industry of'.

senses.def: certain to happen and impossible to stop
ex: Change is inevitable.
The delay was inevitable.

senses.def: too bad to be forgiven or accepted
ex: His rude behaviour was inexcusable.
Being late again is inexcusable.

senses.def: in a way that cannot be stopped or changed
ex: The river moved inexorably towards the sea.
Prices rose inexorably.

senses.def: having little knowledge or experience of something
ex: The team is young and inexperienced.
He was an inexperienced driver.

senses.def: impossible to explain or understand
ex: He left for some inexplicable reason.
The disappearance remains inexplicable.

senses.def: never wrong and never making mistakes
ex: No one is infallible.
The system is not infallible.

senses.def: a baby or very young child
ex: The infant slept in her arms.
Infant mortality has fallen.

senses.def: to give a disease to a person, animal or plant
ex: The virus infected thousands of people.
Dirty water can infect the wound.

senses.def: containing germs that cause disease
ex: The cut became infected.
Infected people should stay at home.

senses.def: an illness caused by germs, or the process of spreading it
ex: He has a chest infection.
Wash your hands to prevent infection.

senses.def: an infectious disease can pass from one person to another
ex: Flu is highly infectious.
Stay at home if you are infectious.

senses.def: spreading quickly from person to person (of feelings)
ex: Her laugh is infectious.

senses.def: extremely annoying (old-fashioned)
ex: Turn off that infernal noise!

senses.def: a general rise in prices over time
ex: Inflation is at three per cent.
High inflation makes life expensive.

senses.def: having a strong effect on people's ideas or decisions
ex: She is an influential writer.
His book was very influential.

senses.def: to tell someone about something officially
ex: Please inform us of any changes.
They informed him that the flight was cancelled.

mistake.wrong: She informed me about that she was late.
mistake.right: She informed me that she was late.
mistake.note: 'Inform' takes a person as its object, then either 'that' or 'of/about'; do not use 'about that'.

senses.def: relaxed and friendly, not formal
ex: It was an informal meeting.
He wrote an informal email.

senses.def: a person who secretly gives information to the police or an organisation
ex: The police received a tip from an informant.

senses.def: facts about a situation, person or event
ex: For more information, visit our website.
I need some information about the course.

mistake.right: I have a lot of information. / I have several pieces of information.
mistake.note: information is uncountable in English, even though معلومات is plural in Arabic.

senses.def: very clever and inventive
ex: It was an ingenious solution to the problem.
She found an ingenious way to save money.

senses.def: skill at thinking of new and clever ways to solve problems
ex: They used ingenuity to fix the engine.
The design shows great ingenuity.

senses.def: a person who does not thank others for their help (formal)
ex: He is an ingrate who forgot all our kindness.

senses.def: one of the foods used to make a dish
ex: Flour and eggs are the main ingredients.
Check the list of ingredients on the packet.

senses.def: one of the parts that make something successful
ex: Hard work is a key ingredient of success.

senses.def: existing as a natural or basic part of something that cannot be removed
ex: Every investment carries inherent risk.
There are dangers inherent in any extreme sport.
Her inherent sense of fairness made her a good judge.

mistake.wrong: The risk is inherent to every plan.
mistake.right: The risk is inherent in every plan.

senses.def: in a way that is a basic or permanent part of something
ex: Some sports are inherently dangerous.
The plan is not inherently bad.

senses.def: to receive money or property from someone who has died
ex: She inherited the house from her aunt.

senses.def: to have the same qualities as your parents
ex: He inherited his father's blue eyes.

senses.def: money or property that you receive when someone dies
ex: He spent his inheritance on a boat.
She received a small inheritance.

senses.def: the first letter of a name
ex: Write your initials at the bottom of the form.

senses.def: happening at the beginning
ex: My initial reaction was surprise.
The initial results look good.

senses.def: at the beginning
ex: Initially, I didn't like the job.
The company initially employed ten people.

senses.def: a new plan or action to solve a problem
ex: The government launched a new health initiative.

senses.def: the ability to decide and act without being told
ex: He showed initiative and fixed the problem himself.
She took the initiative and called him.

senses.def: an act of putting medicine into the body with a needle
ex: The nurse gave him an injection.
She is afraid of injections.

senses.def: physically hurt, especially in an accident
ex: Two injured players left the pitch.
He was seriously injured in the crash.

senses.def: physical harm to a person or animal, especially in an accident
ex: He missed the game because of an injury.
The crash caused serious injuries.

senses.def: unfair treatment, or a situation in which people are treated unfairly
ex: She fought against injustice.
It was a great injustice.

senses.def: coloured liquid used for writing, drawing or printing
ex: The pen ran out of ink.
He wrote the letter in black ink.

senses.def: not having done anything wrong or committed a crime
ex: The man is innocent.
She was found innocent of the crime.

senses.def: not intending to cause harm
ex: It was an innocent mistake.

senses.def: a new idea, method or invention, or the act of creating one
ex: The company is known for innovation.
The phone has many technical innovations.

senses.def: a remark that suggests something unpleasant without saying it directly
ex: The article was full of innuendo about his private life.

senses.def: help, ideas or information that people give to a project
ex: We welcome your input on the plan.
The team's input was very useful.

senses.def: information put into a computer
ex: The program needs input from the user.

senses.def: to ask for information about something
ex: I'm writing to inquire about the course.
She inquired whether the room was free.

mistake.wrong: I inquired him about the price.
mistake.note: Use 'inquire about' + thing; the person is introduced with 'of' or by 'ask'.

senses.def: a question asking for information
ex: I made an inquiry at the desk.
Thank you for your inquiry.

senses.def: an official examination of facts about a problem or event
ex: The government ordered an inquiry into the accident.

senses.def: very silly or crazy (informal)
ex: That idea is insane.
You'd be insane to drive in this storm.

senses.def: suffering from a serious mental illness (old-fashioned)
ex: He was declared insane by the court.

senses.def: impossible to understand because it shows no feelings
ex: His face was calm and inscrutable.
She gave an inscrutable smile.

senses.def: lacking confidence and worried about yourself
ex: He felt insecure about his looks.
Insecure people often compare themselves to others.

senses.def: not safe or protected
ex: The building is insecure at night.

senses.def: not noticing or caring about other people's feelings
ex: It was an insensitive comment.
He was insensitive to her sadness.

senses.def: in or into a place, building or container
ex: Put it inside the box.
He is inside the house.

senses.def: in or into a building or room
ex: It's raining, so let's go inside.
Come inside!

senses.def: on the inner part or side of something
ex: Put the key in the inside pocket.

senses.def: the inner part or surface of something
ex: The inside of the box was red.

senses.def: a clear and deep understanding of something
ex: The book gives a useful insight into life in Japan.
She has great insight into children.

senses.def: showing a clear and deep understanding of a situation
ex: She made an insightful comment.
It was an insightful article.

senses.def: to demand something strongly and refuse to accept no
ex: She insisted on paying for the meal.
I insist that you stay.

senses.def: to say something firmly, especially when others do not believe you
ex: He insists that he is innocent.

mistake.wrong: He insisted to go with us.
mistake.right: He insisted on going with us.
mistake.note: After 'insist on', use a noun or the -ing form, not 'to + verb'.

senses.def: to look at something carefully to check that it is correct or in good condition
ex: The officer inspected our passports.
Engineers inspect the bridge every year.

senses.def: an official visit or careful check to see that things are correct
ex: The restaurant failed its health inspection.
A close inspection showed a small crack.

senses.def: a person whose job is to check that rules are followed
ex: A health inspector visited the kitchen.

senses.def: a police officer of fairly high rank
ex: The inspector questioned the witnesses.

senses.def: to make someone feel they want to do something, or to give them ideas
ex: Her story inspired me to study medicine.
The trip inspired a poem.

senses.def: to fit equipment or a machine in its place so that it can be used
ex: They installed a new heating system.
A man came to install the washing machine.

senses.def: to put a program onto a computer so that it can be used
ex: You need to install the app first.

senses.def: a particular example or case of something
ex: There were several instances of cheating.
For instance, you could take a bus.

senses.def: happening immediately, in less than a second
ex: The reaction was instantaneous.
Light travels at an almost instantaneous speed.

senses.def: immediately, in no time
ex: The message arrived almost instantaneously.

senses.def: immediately
ex: She recognised him instantly.
The driver died instantly.

senses.def: in place of something that was mentioned
ex: I don't want tea. Can I have coffee instead?
He didn't go to school; he stayed at home instead.

mistake.wrong: I stayed at home instead going out.
mistake.right: I stayed at home instead of going out.
mistake.note: Use 'instead of' before a noun or -ing form; 'instead' alone goes at the end or start.

senses.def: a natural way of behaving or knowing without having to think or learn
ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
Trust your instincts.

senses.def: in a way that you do naturally, without thinking
ex: She instinctively stepped back.
He instinctively knew something was wrong.

senses.def: an organisation for education or research
ex: She works at a research institute.
He studies at a language institute.

senses.def: to introduce a system, rule or process (formal)
ex: The school instituted new safety rules.

senses.def: a large organisation such as a bank, school or hospital
ex: Banks are financial institutions.
The university is an old institution.

senses.def: a custom or system that has existed for a long time
ex: Marriage is an important social institution.

senses.def: to tell someone what to do, especially officially
ex: The doctor instructed him to rest.
Officers were instructed to wait.

senses.def: to teach someone a skill or subject
ex: She instructs students in first aid.

senses.def: a person who teaches a practical skill
ex: My driving instructor was very patient.
She is a swimming instructor.

senses.def: refusing to obey someone who has authority over you
ex: The soldier was punished for insubordination.

senses.def: not enough for a particular purpose
ex: There was insufficient evidence.
Their funds were insufficient.

senses.def: a rude or offensive remark or action
ex: He shouted insults at the referee.
I took it as an insult.

senses.def: to say or do something rude that offends someone
ex: I didn't mean to insult you.
She felt insulted by the offer.

senses.def: an agreement in which you pay a company so that it pays you if something bad happens
ex: Do you have car insurance?
The insurance paid for the repairs.

senses.def: being an essential part of something
ex: Exercise is an integral part of my day.
Music is integral to their culture.

senses.def: the process of combining two or more things, or of mixing people into a group
ex: The school helps the integration of new pupils.
The integration of the two systems took a year.

senses.def: the ability to think in a clever, logical way
ex: She has a sharp intellect.
He was admired for his intellect.

senses.def: relating to the ability to think and understand
ex: The job needs a high level of intellectual skill.
He has many intellectual interests.

senses.def: a person who enjoys studying and thinking about complicated ideas
ex: The café was full of writers and intellectuals.

senses.def: the ability to learn, understand and think about things
ex: She showed great intelligence.
Dogs have a high level of intelligence.

senses.def: secret information about a government or enemy
ex: The intelligence service warned the government.

senses.def: to have a plan or aim in your mind
ex: I intend to study law.
She didn't intend to hurt you.

senses.def: very strong or extreme in degree
ex: The heat was intense.
She felt intense pain.

senses.def: serious, with strong feelings
ex: He is a very intense person.

senses.def: giving all your attention to something, or determined to do something
ex: He was intent on winning the race.
The children were intent on their game.

senses.def: a plan or aim to do something
ex: I have no intention of leaving.
She had good intentions.

senses.def: deliberately, not by accident
ex: He intentionally broke the window.
I didn't do it intentionally.

senses.def: the feeling of wanting to know or learn about something
ex: She has a great interest in history.
He lost interest in the game.

senses.def: an activity that you enjoy
ex: My interests include music and cooking.

senses.def: extra money paid on a loan or earned on savings
ex: The bank charges high interest on loans.

senses.def: to make someone want to know more about something
ex: History interests me a lot.
Does the job interest you?

mistake.note: Use 'interested' for how a person feels, and 'interesting' for the thing that causes the feeling.

senses.def: to try to influence a situation that is not your business
ex: Don't interfere in other people's lives.
Her parents never interfere.

senses.def: to stop something from working or happening properly
ex: Noise interferes with my work.

senses.def: the inside part of a building, car or other object
ex: The interior of the house is modern.
The car has a leather interior.

senses.def: fitting closely together so that parts connect
ex: The floor is made of interlocking tiles.
Interlocking pieces make up the puzzle.

senses.def: a short period between two events, or a short performance between parts of a longer show
ex: The holiday was a pleasant interlude in a busy year.
A song was played during the interlude.

senses.def: a person who helps two sides to communicate or reach an agreement
ex: The lawyer acted as an intermediary between them.

senses.def: inside something, especially a body or an organisation
ex: He had internal injuries.
The company has an internal phone system.

senses.def: involving more than one country
ex: She works for an international company.
We took an international flight.

senses.def: to decide what you think something means
ex: How do you interpret this poem?
She interpreted his silence as a yes.

senses.def: to translate speech from one language to another
ex: He interpreted for the visiting president.

senses.def: an explanation of what something means
ex: There are many interpretations of this poem.
Your interpretation of the data is wrong.

senses.def: a person whose job is to translate speech from one language into another
ex: The president spoke through an interpreter.

senses.def: to ask someone many questions for a long time, often in an aggressive way
ex: Police interrogated the suspect for hours.

senses.def: a long period of questioning, especially by the police
ex: He was taken away for interrogation.
The interrogation lasted all night.

senses.def: to stop someone while they are speaking or doing something
ex: Please don't interrupt me.
A phone call interrupted our meal.

senses.def: something that stops a process for a short time
ex: I work best without interruptions.
There was a brief interruption in the broadcast.

senses.def: a place where two or more roads cross
ex: Turn left at the next intersection.
There was an accident at the intersection.

senses.def: very close and personal
ex: They are intimate friends.
He told her intimate details about his life.

senses.def: private and friendly in feeling
ex: We had dinner in an intimate restaurant.

senses.def: towards the inside of something
ex: She walked into the room.
Put the milk into the cup.

senses.def: used to show a change from one state to another
ex: Water turns into ice.
Cut the cake into six pieces.

mistake.note: Use 'into' (not 'in') to show movement towards the inside.

senses.def: being a basic and important part of something
ex: The intrinsic value of the painting is high.
Risk is intrinsic to business.

senses.def: the first part of a book, speech or piece of writing
ex: Read the introduction first.
The book has a short introduction.

senses.def: the act of telling two people each other's names when they first meet
ex: Let me make the introductions.

senses.def: the start of something new
ex: The introduction of the new tax caused anger.

senses.def: to enter or become involved where you are not wanted
ex: I'm sorry to intrude on your meeting.
Journalists intruded on the family's grief.

senses.def: a person who goes into a place without permission
ex: The dog barked at the intruder.
An intruder broke into the shop.

senses.def: the act of entering a place or situation where you are not wanted
ex: She felt the visit was an intrusion.
The film is an intrusion into their private lives.

senses.def: the ability to know something without thinking or learning about it
ex: My intuition told me something was wrong.
She chose the job by intuition.

senses.def: based on feelings rather than facts
ex: She has an intuitive understanding of people.
The app is intuitive and easy to use.

senses.def: the act of entering a country with an army to take control
ex: The invasion began at dawn.
Many people fled the invasion.

senses.def: an unwanted entry into something private
ex: It was an invasion of privacy.

senses.def: a person who has made or thought of something completely new
ex: He was the inventor of the telephone.
She is a young inventor.

senses.def: to put money into something to make a profit later
ex: He invested his savings in a small business.
Many people invest in property.

senses.def: to spend time or effort on something to get a good result
ex: She invested a lot of time in her studies.

senses.def: to examine a crime, problem or event to find out the truth
ex: Police are investigating the robbery.
Scientists investigated the cause of the fire.

senses.def: an official examination of the facts about a crime or problem
ex: The investigation took six months.
Police have launched an investigation.

senses.def: a person whose job is to find out the facts about a crime or event
ex: A private investigator was hired.
Investigators found no evidence.

senses.def: money put into something to make a profit, or the thing you put money in
ex: A house can be a good investment.
The firm needs more investment.

senses.def: a person who puts money into a business to make a profit
ex: Investors are worried about the economy.
The company is looking for new investors.

senses.def: impossible to see
ex: Germs are invisible to the eye.
In the story, he wears an invisible cloak.

senses.def: a request to come to an event or place, or the card or message that asks you
ex: Thank you for the invitation.
I sent invitations to all my friends.

senses.def: to ask someone to come to an event or place
ex: She invited me to her party.
We invited them for dinner.

senses.def: a document that lists goods or services you have provided and the money to be paid
ex: Please send the invoice to our office.
The invoice is due next week.

senses.def: to have something as a necessary part
ex: The job involves travelling.
What does the course involve?

senses.def: to make someone take part in something
ex: Don't involve me in your argument.

senses.def: taking part in something, or connected with it
ex: Many students are involved in the project.
I don't want to get involved.

senses.def: the fact of taking part in something, or being connected with it
ex: Parents' involvement helps children learn.
He denied any involvement in the crime.

senses.def: a hard grey metal used to make tools and machines
ex: The gate is made of iron.
Spinach contains iron.

senses.def: an electrical tool with a flat bottom used to make clothes smooth
ex: Switch off the iron when you finish.

senses.def: to make clothes smooth with an iron
ex: I need to iron my shirt.
She irons every Sunday.

senses.def: strange or funny because it is the opposite of what you would expect
ex: It was ironic that the fire station caught fire.
He gave an ironic smile.

senses.def: in a way that is strange because it is the opposite of what you would expect
ex: Ironically, the doctor was the one who fell ill.
She said it ironically.

senses.def: a situation that is strange because it is the opposite of what you expect
ex: The irony is that he hated the job he fought for.
She spoke with irony.

senses.def: not based on clear thought or reason
ex: He has an irrational fear of spiders.
Her anger was irrational.

senses.def: so attractive or strong that you cannot say no
ex: The cake smelled irresistible.
I felt an irresistible urge to laugh.

senses.def: not thinking about the effect of your actions on others
ex: It was irresponsible to leave the children alone.
He is an irresponsible driver.

senses.def: impossible to change or cancel
senses.ar: لا رجعة فيه؛ غير قابل للإلغاء
ex: It was an irrevocable decision.
The damage is irrevocable.

senses.def: in a way that cannot be changed or cancelled
ex: Their friendship was irrevocably damaged.

senses.def: annoyed or a little angry
ex: She was irritated by his constant questions.
He sounded irritated.

senses.def: making you feel annoyed
ex: He has an irritating habit of tapping his pen.
The noise is really irritating.

senses.def: the form of 'be' used with he, she and it
ex: She is a teacher.
It is cold today.

senses.def: used with an -ing form or past participle to make continuous and passive forms
ex: He is reading a book.
The window is broken.

mistake.wrong: She is a teacher and is lives here.
mistake.right: She is a teacher and lives here.
mistake.note: Do not use 'is' before another main verb; Arabic has no verb 'to be' in the present, so learners sometimes add or omit it.

senses.def: to keep a person or thing separate from others
ex: Sick patients are isolated to stop the disease spreading.
The storm isolated the village.

senses.def: far from other places or people
ex: They live in an isolated village.
She felt isolated in the new city.

senses.def: happening only once
ex: It was an isolated incident.

senses.def: the state of being separate from others
ex: Many old people suffer from isolation.
The patient was kept in isolation.

senses.def: a subject or problem that people discuss
ex: Climate change is an important issue.
Let's talk about the issue of money.

senses.def: a copy of a magazine or newspaper published at a particular time
ex: I bought the latest issue.

senses.def: to officially give out or announce something
ex: The government issued a warning.
They issued new passports.

senses.def: used for a thing, animal or situation already mentioned
ex: I have a dog. It is very friendly.
Where is my phone? I can't find it.

senses.def: used as a subject for weather, time and distance
ex: It is raining.
It is six o'clock.

senses.def: the player who has to catch the others in a children's game
ex: You're it!

mistake.wrong: My car is old. Is very slow.
mistake.right: My car is old. It is very slow.
mistake.note: English needs a subject such as 'it' in every sentence, while Arabic can leave it out.

senses.def: to have an uncomfortable feeling on the skin that makes you want to scratch
ex: My arm itches.
The wool sweater makes me itch.

senses.def: a plan of a journey, including the places you will visit
ex: Our itinerary includes three cities.
I sent you the full itinerary.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with a thing or animal already mentioned
ex: The dog wagged its tail.
The company changed its name.

senses.def: used in a few phrases as a possessive pronoun (rare)
ex: This house has seen its better days.

mistake.note: 'Its' shows possession; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'.

senses.def: used when a thing or animal does something to its own self
ex: The cat washed itself.
The door closed by itself.

senses.def: used to stress a particular thing
ex: The idea itself is good, but the plan is not.
